chapter: Players and bands of old New Orleans
title: Barney Bigard, Albert Nicholas and Dominique
summary: He says he helped Albert Nicholas read music before he and Bigard left together, and mentions the Dominique cousins.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Yeah. But, um, he was talking about, uh, Albert, he was talking about. Yeah, Albert.

Schneider. Oh, yes. Yeah, Albert. He was like, from here too, Albert. Yes, I never met him. Now, you see, Bonnie. Yeah. Bonnie Bigot come from under the same man, I come from Teal. The Teal. Uh-huh. He was like, I'm the fellow, help Albert Nicholas to read music so he could go away with Bonnie. By the time they left here, they was playing that Tom Anderson. Mm-hmm. They left together in the bunch of cover. Him and Albert Nicholas together. Both clarinet players. Mm-hmm. They left together, him and Bonnie. How did Barney play when he was here? Was he good on clarinet when... Well, at that time, Bonnie was way behind me.
Yeah, he was way behind me. He wasn't up much. I heard... He was bashful. He was too bashful.
I heard he played saxophone mostly down here, I guess, did he? Yeah, he was bashful. He didn't do much playing. He took like Albert Dominic. Oh, yeah. That's my voice good cousin too.
When they call Don Albert now. Don Albert trumpet bell. Yeah, yeah. That's my question.
I know Nanny Dominic very well in Chicago. Yeah, Nanny Dominic. I must see, is his brother still living, I guess, Ferdinand Dominic?
